# [2.4.0](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/compare/v2.3.0...v2.4.0) (2026-08-13)

### Features

* **frontend:** add Sentry and PostHog with a hard privacy boundary ([8728e87](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/commit/8728e8762de83c4e9e2c434f76de9f74590c265f))
* **frontend:** add WalletConnect for mobile and hardware wallets ([9c7c57d](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/commit/9c7c57d7819ade9fd3de67830dd564a070d3b383))

feat(frontend): add WalletConnect for mobile and hardware wallets

window.ethereum only ever reaches a desktop browser extension, which excludes
phone wallets and hardware devices — most of the people who actually care
about a stop nobody can see.

The connect flow now offers a choice, and whichever provider connects is kept
in state so sealing, cancelling and the network switch all speak through the
same transport rather than falling back to window.ethereum. Kept viem and did
not pull in wagmi or rainbowkit: the app has one connect call and one chain,
so a connector framework would be more code than it removes.

The SDK is imported lazily, so users on an injected wallet never download it.
With NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID unset the option is hidden and the
injected path behaves exactly as before, so local dev needs no account.

Co-Authored-By: google-labs-jules[bot] <161369871+google-labs-jules[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(frontend): add Sentry and PostHog with a hard privacy boundary

Error tracking and funnel analytics, both no-ops when their env vars are
unset so local dev and CI stay clean and account-free.

The interesting part is what must never be sent. Payloads are scrubbed of
0x-hex, bare hex runs and XRPL addresses before leaving the browser — but
that alone was not enough, and testing found the hole: a trigger price is a
plain decimal like "2.5", which no value-level pattern can tell apart from a
legitimate metric.

So keys that could carry order terms are now dropped outright, at any nesting
depth, rather than value-scrubbed. A denylist is usually the weaker choice;
the alternative here was scrubbing every number, which would make analytics
useless. Call sites only send named funnel events, so this is a backstop
against a future change widening a payload by accident.

Two tests lock it in: no term-bearing key survives, and legitimate fields
(event name, walletConnected) do. 18 frontend tests pass.

Also stops tracking frontend/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, a build artifact that
should never have been committed.

Co-Authored-By: google-labs-jules[bot] <161369871+google-labs-jules[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

feat(keeper): add telegram notifications on successful order execution

- POSTs to Telegram Bot API sendMessage with order ID, action, and explorer tx link upon successful execute() transaction receipt.
- Decodes action from ABI-encoded resultData.
- Configurable via optional TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID env variables.
- Silently skips when environment variables are unset.
- Ensures order terms or trigger prices are never included in the notification message.
- Adds comprehensive node:test coverage in keeper/test/lib.test.js.

# [2.2.0](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/compare/v2.1.1...v2.2.0) (2026-08-13)

### Features

* **extension:** add OCO bracket orders and lock in tick indistinguishability ([687dfdc](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/commit/687dfdc239ab109bf775ee4fdb82cbb89182dbcf))

feat(extension): add OCO bracket orders and lock in tick indistinguishability

A bracket is a stop and a take-profit sharing one escrow, expressed as an
optional second threshold inside the same encrypted payload. Whichever side
hits first settles the order, and the contract's existing executed flag kills
the other leg — so this needs no second order, no cancellation path, and no
contract change at all.

Publicly this is exactly the order type you cannot place safely: a public
bracket leaks both your downside limit and your upside target. Sealed, it
leaks neither.

Written test-first. The wire format is the risk here, so two tests guard it:
the take-profit leg must survive an encode/decode round trip, and a zero must
decode to "no bracket" rather than a take-profit at price zero — which would
make every single-leg stop fire instantly.

Also added tests asserting no-op and fired ticks are indistinguishable by
status, and that the enclave log never mentions the threshold or how near the
price is. Both already passed: the design had the property, nothing enforced
it. Dummy-tick generation was considered and skipped — it would add
complexity to buy a property already held, and these tests now stop a future
change from silently losing it.

## [2.1.1](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/compare/v2.1.0...v2.1.1) (2026-08-12)

### Bug Fixes

* **frontend:** never let a decorative animation hide content ([5dd7b73](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/commit/5dd7b7346bd9fe69df3425e25d5d89c8e4968dd7))

fix(frontend): never let a decorative animation hide content

The scroll reveal held every element at opacity 0 until animation machinery
reported in. Measured in a real browser, neither the IntersectionObserver
version nor the native scroll-timeline replacement ever advanced there, so
all 14 targets stayed fully transparent — a blank page.

A decorative effect must not be able to hide content, so it is removed
rather than repaired. Motion stays where it cannot cause harm: the cipher
scramble, hover and press states, and the hero rule.

Also fixes the step offset, which .reveal[data-shown] was silently
cancelling by setting transform:none at higher specificity; it now uses
margin so the two cannot collide.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# [2.1.0](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/compare/v2.0.0...v2.1.0) (2026-08-12)

### Features

* **frontend:** split landing from app, add navigation and scroll reveals ([4582f12](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/commit/4582f123eec238334c6f16c443958ced2f65c84d))

feat(frontend): split landing from app, add navigation and scroll reveals

Everything previously lived on one page, so a trader arriving cold met an
order form with no explanation of what it was for. Now `/` argues the
product and `/app` is the working order book, joined by a sticky nav.

The landing leads with the actual claim — your stop-loss is public right
now — and closes on what Wraith deliberately does not do, because on a
privacy product the disclaimed scope is the credibility.

Choices worth recording:

- The hero artifact is a live-scrambling cipher block rather than stock
  photography. Every field of the example order is legible except the
  condition, which is the whole product stated visually. It is memoized and
  isolated so its interval never re-renders the page.
- Reveals use IntersectionObserver, not a scroll listener and not GSAP. The
  question is only "has this entered view", which the browser answers off
  the main thread, and the transition stays on transform/opacity.
- The nav gains its surface from a sentinel element rather than a scroll
  handler, so there is no per-frame main-thread work.
- The three steps are deliberately offset rather than three equal columns.

Kept vanilla CSS rather than migrating to Tailwind, and kept Archivo rather
than switching to Geist — Geist is now the common default and would read as
more generic, not less.

Verified: both routes build and serve, heading order is h1/h2/h3 with a
single h1, 14 reveal targets mount, no emoji in output, no 100vh anywhere,
and reduced-motion is honoured in three places.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(contracts)!: take TEE authority from the registry, not the owner

execute() now asks TeeMachineRegistry.getActiveTeeMachines(extensionId)
whether the recovered signer is a TEE registered to this extension, and the
owner-curated allowlist is deleted along with setTeeAddress().

The earlier code used an allowlist because ITeeMachineRegistry was documented
as exposing only getRandomTeeIds — a random selector, not a membership query.
That was wrong: the scaffold's own extension-post-setup.sh reads the TEE
signing address from getActiveTeeMachines, and the function is live on the
Coston2 FlareTeeManager diamond. Probing it directly settled the question.

This removes a real trust assumption rather than documenting one. The
contract owner can no longer authorize a signer of their choosing, and a
test asserts that even the owner cannot. Retiring a machine in the registry
revokes its ability to settle immediately, with no action needed here.

Written test-first: the four new tests failed with "bad TEE signature"
against the allowlist implementation before the registry lookup existed.

BREAKING CHANGE: setTeeAddress(address,bool) is removed. Deployments no
longer register a TEE signer; registry registration is the only step.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: wire and record the live FAssets and swap addresses

setAssetManager and setRouter are now called on the deployed contract, so
both settlement paths are live rather than unconfigured:

  AssetManagerFXRP  0xc1Ca88b937d0b528842F95d5731ffB586f4fbDFA
  FXRP              0x0b6A3645c240605887a5532109323A3E12273dc7
  BlazeSwap router  0x8D29b61C41CF318d15d031BE2928F79630e068e6

AssetManagerFXRP was resolved live from the FlareContractRegistry rather
than copied from docs, and its fAsset() returns exactly the FXRP address
the docs list — the two agree, so neither is stale. The runbook now shows

## [1.3.1](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/compare/v1.3.0...v1.3.1) (2026-08-12)

### Bug Fixes

* **frontend:** allow .ts import extensions so the build type-checks ([7062f33](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/commit/7062f330af226bc15ae59963aa88231112621d54))

fix(frontend): allow .ts import extensions so the build type-checks

The new test file imports './wraith.ts' with an explicit extension because
node --experimental-strip-types resolves ESM imports literally. Next's build
type-checks every file in tsconfig, so that extension failed the build with
TS5097 and left no .next directory to serve.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: record the live Coston2 deployment

WraithOrders is deployed at 0x174107F5bE6cd1d1c00A83273286a89623D02b81.
The README now carries the address, deploy tx, and the FCC registry and
FtsoV2 addresses it talks to, plus a diagram of where the plaintext lives.

Notes that the contract's OP_TYPE_WRAITH and OP_COMMAND_EVAL_ORDER decode
onchain to WRAITH and EVAL_ORDER, matching the Go constants byte for byte —
the invariant FCC instruction routing depends on, checked against the live
contract rather than assumed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(frontend): cover the price-parsing money path

priceToE18 converts what a trader types into the 1e18 threshold the enclave
compares against, so a scale error fires an order at the wrong price. It had
no tests.

Every test here was mutation-checked rather than trusted because it passed:
left-aligning the fraction (turning 0.05 into 0.5, a 10x trigger error) fails
5 tests, dropping the whitespace trim fails 1, dropping the 18-decimal
truncation fails 6, and hiding formatCipher's withheld-byte count fails 1.
All four mutants die, so the suite catches real defects rather than
restating the implementation.

Runs on the built-in node:test runner via --experimental-strip-types — no
new dependencies — and is now wired into CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(deploy): record the real Coston2 FCC registry address

Both registry constructor args are the FlareTeeManager diamond proxy at
0x1a9C4A0f9D76c0b1D91d22E24E573a9b377618aE — the diamond serves the
extension-registry and machine-registry facets from one address, which the
scaffold confirms in tools/pkg/utils/instructions.go. The deploy script and
runbook previously left these as placeholders.

# [1.3.0](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/compare/v1.2.0...v1.3.0) (2026-08-12)

### Features

* **frontend:** production polish — container, stats, network guard, states ([647b8d6](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/commit/647b8d65e31c8488ddff72f575f79a514a281575))

docs: add contributing guide, security policy, issue and PR templates

Encodes the invariants that are not style preferences — order plaintext
never leaving the browser or enclave, byte-identical OPType strings, the
dependency-free trigger core, and execute() verification never being
weakened — so contributors and reviewers see them before they break one.

SECURITY.md states plainly that this is Coston2-only and points
vulnerability reports at private advisories rather than public issues.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(frontend): production polish — container, stats, network guard, states

Design audit against the taste-skill checklist, and the fixes it surfaced:

Layout — there was no max-width container, so on a wide monitor the panels
sat in a narrow strip with dead space beside them. A single .shell governs
every band now, giving the page one spine.

Real data — a stat row computes orders created, currently sealed, fired, and
total FXRP in escrow from the same on-chain reads that build the list. No
invented figures.

Functionality — wrong-network detection with a one-click switch (falling back
to addChain when Coston2 is not in the wallet yet), All/Mine order filtering,
and XRPL address and day-count input validation.

States — skeleton cards that match the real card's shape instead of a
spinner, per-card staggered entry, press feedback on every control, and
transitions on inputs. Reduced-motion silences all of it.

Missing pieces — favicon, branded 404, footer with source and trust-doc
links, skip-to-content link, and OpenGraph/Twitter metadata.

Surface — fixed grain overlay and violet-tinted shadows, because large flat
dark fields read as plastic without texture.

Verified: builds clean, and the rendered markup carries the shell, grain,
stats, skeletons, footer, skip link, working 404 and favicon.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(keeper): extract pure helpers and cover them with node:test

Pulls the keeper's response handling out of the network path so it can be
tested without a proxy: handleFetchResultResponse (404, still-processing,
missing status, non-OK, and success cases) and determineRelayAction (which
results are worth relaying and which are no-ops). Nine tests on the built-in
node:test runner, no new dependencies.

Also wires keeper and frontend jobs into CI, which previously only ran
contracts and extension.

Dropped the PendingBookkeeper class from the generated patch: it wrapped a
Map and reimplemented has/get/size/delete with set renamed to add, and
nothing outside its own test called those methods. A plain Map does the job.

# [1.2.0](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.0) (2026-08-11)

### Features

* **frontend:** add live FTSO ticker, on-chain activity log and mechanism rail ([48e8c50](https://github.com/LSUDOKO/Wraith/commit/48e8c50c1d83786ef53afef67854581479f764d1))

feat(frontend): add live FTSO ticker, on-chain activity log and mechanism rail

All real data, nothing synthesized:
- The ticker reads FLR/XRP/BTC/ETH-USD block-latency feeds live from
  FtsoV2 on Coston2 every 10s — the same oracle surface the enclave reads
  during evaluation, so what the strip shows is what the TEE would see on
  the next tick.
- The activity log renders Wraith's own on-chain events (created, ticked,
  executed, cancelled) from the last ~70k blocks as an operations feed. The
  conspicuous absence is the point: no line ever names a trigger price.
- The masthead's dead right half becomes a Seal/Watch/Fire mechanism rail —
  a real on-chain sequence, so the numbering is earned.

Verified in Chrome at desktop and 400px mobile widths; live quotes observed
updating between screenshots.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(frontend): add cancel, explorer links and live order refresh

Owners can cancel a sealed order from its card (escrow refunds on-chain);
every owner address and the last transaction link out to the Coston2
explorer; and the order list refreshes every 15s because executions and
cancellations land from other actors — the keeper, other wallets — not only
from this page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(extension): add enclave runtime — ABI codecs, FTSO reader, decrypt client, handler

Completes the extension beyond the pure trigger core:

- Hand-rolled ABI codecs for the three fixed Wraith layouts (instruction,
  sealed terms, settlement result) rather than importing go-ethereum — the
  layouts are fixed by the contract and a dependency-light enclave image is
  easier to reproduce and audit. Truncation and malformed-word cases tested.
- FtsoReader does eth_call from inside the enclave with a runtime-computed
  selector (cannot silently drift from the signature) and folds Solidity's
  sign-extended int8 decimals correctly.
- Decryptor wraps the TEE node's /decrypt endpoint; the enclave key never
  leaves the node.
- Handler ties them together and enforces two properties with tests:
  a sealed order is bound to the contract named inside its terms, so a
  ciphertext cannot be replayed through another deployment's tick(); and
  the settlement result carries no trace of the threshold or direction —
  a test asserts the secret bytes do not appear in the output.

The no-op and fired paths share status 1 deliberately, so nothing outside
the enclave can distinguish them until a result is relayed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(contracts): add Deploy script and Coston2 deployment runbook

Deploy.s.sol reads the FCC registry addresses from the environment (FCC is
pre-release; they live in the scaffold's deployed-addresses.json, not the
FlareContractRegistry yet) and optionally wires the BlazeSwap router and
FXRP AssetManager. docs/DEPLOY.md is the sequential runbook from indexer
credentials through smoke test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: add AGENTS.md for Google Jules and other coding agents

Jules reads AGENTS.md for repo context and environment setup. Encodes the
project invariant (order plaintext exists only in the browser and the
enclave), the byte-identical OPType/OPCommand rule, the dependency-free
trigger-core rule, and the verification commands agents must run before
claiming work done.

commit.message:
feat(frontend): add order composer that seals conditions client-side

Encrypts an order's terms in the browser and stores only the ciphertext
on-chain. The enclave public key is fetched through a server-side /api/info
route rather than from the browser, because the extension proxy sets no CORS
headers and its tunnel URL should not ship in a client bundle.

Design is a darkroom safelight: violet-cast ink, one amber signal colour,
and mono type reserved exclusively for cipher bytes so the unreadable
material reads as the most privileged thing on the page. The seal — an order's
hex block under a slow safelight sweep — is the signature element, and the
layout's argument is the contrast around it: everything about an order is
legible except the one thing that matters. Form fields whose values get
encrypted carry an amber border so what stays secret is visible at a glance.

Not visually verified — no browser was available in this environment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(keeper): add permissionless tick and relay loop

Pokes live orders so the TEE re-evaluates their conditions, then relays
TEE-signed results to execute().

The keeper is untrusted by construction. It forwards ciphertext it cannot
read, and the TEE reads FTSO itself rather than trusting a price supplied
here, so the worst a hostile keeper can do is withhold ticks — which is why
ticking is open to anyone and any keeper can cover for another.

Instruction ids come from decoding OrderTicked with viem's parseEventLogs
rather than matching a hand-computed topic hash.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(extension): add TEE-side trigger evaluator

The enclave-side decision logic: given decrypted order terms and an FTSO
reading, decide whether the private condition has fired.

internal/trigger is pure and dependency-free. The decision that moves
someone's money is the part most worth testing, and keeping it free of the
TEE harness means it can be tested without a TEE, a chain, or a network.

Behavioural choices that are easy to get wrong, so each has a test:
- Threshold boundaries are inclusive. A stop set at exactly the traded price
  fires, which is what "stop at X" means to a trader.
- Feed decimals are normalized to 1e18, so the same threshold works against
  any feed and the decision cannot depend on a feed's precision.
- Stale prices refuse to fire rather than firing on old data. Missing a tick
  costs nothing; the keeper ticks again seconds later. An irreversible trade
  on a stale price cannot be undone.
- Out-of-range feed decimals are rejected before exponentiation, so a corrupt
  int8 cannot induce a huge big.Int allocation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(contracts): add WraithOrders private conditional order contract

Escrows an asset alongside an ECIES ciphertext of the trigger condition, so
the condition is never readable on-chain. A keeper pokes the order with
tick(); the TEE extension decrypts and evaluates in-enclave and returns a
signed result only when the condition fires. execute() verifies that
signature and settles via swap or FXRP redemption.

Signature verification follows the FCC ActionResult scheme: rebuild
ActionResult.Hash(), wrap it in the chain-scoped TEE_ACTION_RESULT payload,
and ecrecover under the EIP-191 prefix.

Two hardenings over the reference weather-insurance example:
- actionId is consumed once, so a signed result cannot be replayed to
  execute the same order twice.
- TEE signers are an allowlist rather than a single owner-set address.
  ITeeMachineRegistry exposes only getRandomTeeIds, a random selector
  rather than a membership query, so there is no published way to ask
  whether an address is a registered TEE. The allowlist is the honest
  substitute and is documented as such.

12 Foundry tests cover escrow, valid settlement, forged signatures, replay,
cross-deployment result reuse, expiry, cancellation and tick rate limiting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: scaffold repo with CI, Dependabot and semantic-release

Sets up the project skeleton and release automation before any feature
work lands.

- Dependabot across github-actions, npm (root/frontend/keeper) and gomod
  (extension), with Next/React and viem/wagmi grouped so related bumps
  land together rather than as build-breaking partial upgrades.
- semantic-release on main: version, changelog and GitHub release are
  derived from Conventional Commit messages.
- CI runs forge build/test for contracts and go vet/test -race for the
  extension.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
